To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the turmoil in money market turbulence in the second half 2007 spilled over to FX and long term cross basis swap markets.

(i) the turmoil in US money markets in the last months of 2007 was transmitted to FX swap and cross currency basis swap market, (ii) the use of these swap markets as a way to overcome US dollar shortage funding problems by non US financial firms resulted in marked deviations of FX swap rates from covered interest parity and in the impairment of liquidity of these swap markets, (iii) these deviations were most pronounced in the cross currency basis swap rates of currencies that had the largest US dollar shortage
the turmoil in money market rates in the second half 2007 resulted in a marked deterioration in the functioning of FX swap and cross currency basis swap market.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spillover effects of the money market crisis on the FX swap and cross currency swap markets in 2007 and 2008.
the following question: What is the impact of the turmoil in short term US dollar money markets on the FX swap and long-term cross currency swap markets?
the following issues: • The extent to which the turmoil in US money markets in the summer of 2007 was reflected in FX swaps and cross currency basis swaps markets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the turmoil in the money markets has had a significant effect on the FX swap and long cross currency basis swap market.

(1) the turmoil in money market rates was transmitted to FX swap rates, (2) the transmission of the turbulence to cross currency swap rates is more difficult to establish due to the presence of a number of other drivers of these rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the turmoil in the US money market was the trigger for the turmoil in the FX and cross currency swap markets.

the use of FX swap markets by banks to overcome funding constraints in the second half on 2007 resulted in the breakdown of covered interest parity and the impairment of market liquidity in FX swaps and cross currency basis swaps.
the turmoil in US money markets in the latter part of 2007 had a significant impact on the liquidity of swap markets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the turmoil in money market was a major contributor to the impairment of FX swap and cross currency swap markets.
the use of the FX swap market by non US financials as a means to overcome dollar funding shortages was not without costs.

, in the absence of a coordinated response from the central banks, the turbulence in US money markets in 2007 was transmitted to the FX swap and cross currency basis markets and resulted in a significant impairment of liquidity.
